source.title: Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths?
source.text: The emergence of powerful vibe-coding agents and tools like Reverse Engineer Anything has caused chaos in the music gear world , leaving companies scrambling to figure out how to respond. While some, like Roland, have remained silent for now, others have embraced the modding community. In the last several weeks, as it's become clear that no piece of music gear is safe from Claude and a subreddit full of curious tinkerers, companies have begun making more and more of their devices open source. draft.threads_post:
Vibe-coding tools and Claude are pushing music gear makers to open-source their devices.

Tinkerers on Reddit are using tools like Reverse Engineer Anything to dissect hardware. While Roland has stayed silent, other synth makers are joining the modding community. The biggest move comes from inMusic, parent company of Akai, Moog, and Native Instruments, which is opening up its hardware.

Should synth companies open-source their gear or fight modders?
